themes_detail.label: Illegal tree damage spike
themes_detail.summary: THIS WEEK, Community District 502 received 8 complaints about illegal tree damage, a 814% spike versus the 0.9 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 9.13), suggesting either coordinated unauthorized tree removal or a single major incident affecting multiple residents.
evidence: 8 illegal tree damage complaints last week vs. 0.9 average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 9.13 indicates extreme statistical anomaly
Sustained complaints suggest pattern rather than isolated incident
reporting_angles: Investigate whether complaints cluster geographically—possible single development or contractor removing trees without permits
Interview affected residents and DOE/DPR to determine if illegal tree removal is linked to the 5 active land use applications currently in review

themes_detail.label: Unsanitary conditions surge
themes_detail.summary: THIS WEEK, unsanitary condition complaints reached 11 in Community District 502, up 132% from the 4.8 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 6.45), indicating emerging sanitation failures in streets, parks, or commercial areas.
evidence: 11 unsanitary condition complaints this week vs. 4.8 weekly average
Converges with 4 dumpster complaints this week (967% spike) suggesting waste management breakdown
reporting_angles: Map complaint locations to identify if failures are concentrated in specific neighborhoods or tied to a particular DSNY facility or contractor
Check whether dumpster spike (4 complaints this week vs. 0.4 avg) reflects inadequate waste collection or illegal dumping

themes_detail.label: Elevator outages spike
themes_detail.summary: THIS WEEK, elevator complaints reached 4 in Community District 502, a 1500% spike versus the 0.2 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 8.66), affecting building accessibility for elderly and disabled residents.
evidence: 4 elevator complaints this week vs. 0.2 average over prior 8 weeks
Coincides with 23 general construction/plumbing complaints last week (247% spike), possibly indicating building-wide infrastructure failures
reporting_angles: Determine if elevator outages are concentrated in public housing or senior buildings where accessibility failures have immediate safety impact
Cross-reference with construction spike to see if building work has triggered mechanical failures

themes_detail.label: Street signs disappearing
themes_detail.summary: THIS WEEK, missing street sign complaints reached 6 in Community District 502, an 860% spike versus the 0.6 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 7.72), creating navigation hazards and possible traffic safety risks.
evidence: 6 missing street sign complaints this week vs. 0.6 weekly average
Part of broader infrastructure degradation pattern (also seeing lot condition, street condition spikes)
reporting_angles: Verify whether signs were damaged by weather, vandalism, or DOT maintenance backlog
Check if missing signs correlate with specific corridors or intersections with known traffic or pedestrian safety issues

themes_detail.label: Construction and plumbing surge
themes_detail.summary: LAST WEEK, general construction and plumbing complaints reached 23 in Community District 502, a 247% spike versus the 6.6 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 8.47), suggesting either a major project creating disturbance or widespread building system failures.
evidence: 23 construction/plumbing complaints last week vs. 6.6 weekly average
5 active land use applications and 562 DOB permits filed in district over 90 days; 26 demolitions and 110 new buildings in pipeline suggest active development pressure
reporting_angles: Cross-reference complaints with the 336 Meredith Avenue fleet maintenance facility ULURP and other active projects to see if one project is generating multiple complaints
Interview residents about construction noise, dust, and traffic impacts; check if complaints cluster around specific project sites
